scope: Representative running Arabic body sukuns on seven currently integrated PDF pages; basmala exceptions checked separately. Not whole source certification.

observations.observedShape: Two upward-converging strokes with open bottom, Λ-like wedge, above target body letters. No enclosing ring.
observations.interpretation: Existing source transcription uses U+0652 for these observed body marks; font rendering may use a source-compatible wedge while preserving Unicode.

observations.observedShape: Purple basmala has hooked/loop-like small marks over sin/ha/ya, visually distinct from the running body Λ wedges. They are not the same plain wedge form.
observations.recommendation: Keep basmala out of a blanket running-body sukun font change; exact decorative form remains separately unverified.

observations.observedShape: Damma remains a loop-with-tail/waw-like sign (e.g الحمدُ, الكتابُ, همُ); shadda, fatha, dagger alif, tanwin and stop signs have distinct forms. Circled instruction-band wedges are a separate annotation class.
observations.recommendation: Change only the font outline selected by U+0652 in running body. Do not replace all circle-looking signs, alter Arabic text, or edit upper annotations.
